description: Scoped filesystem storage — a smart notebook for durable LLM artifacts. CALL SHAPE: every storage op is invoked as {"method":"storage_<op>","payload":{...args}} — ALL parameters go inside payload, NOT as top-level arguments. If you get 'args.X is required', you almost certainly put args at the wrong nesting level — wrap them in payload. FULL TOOL CATALOG (18 ops): storage_stat, storage_read, storage_readMany, storage_write, storage_import, storage_list, storage_recent, storage_move, storage_restore, storage_delete, storage_search, storage_copy, storage_append, storage_replace, storage_find, storage_grep, storage_batch, storage_resources_list/read/templates. ⚡ BATCHING RULE: multi-file workflows MUST use storage.import (bulk write) / storage.readMany (bulk read) / storage.batch (mixed ops) — ONE call, never one per file. EDITING CHEATSHEET: targeted text edit = storage_replace (marker+replacement, aliases oldString/newString) — pre-flight with storage_find; add to end = storage_append; full rewrite = storage_write; locate text = storage_grep (regex, line numbers) or storage_find (exact string); undo = copy the file to <root>\temp\* first, then copy it back to roll back (see TEMP below). Backed by the path in config.json agents.storage.root (default: D:\MCP_Storage). When agents.storage.uncShare is also configured, callers may pass EITHER the local path or the UNC share form — the server translates UNC to local before resolving, so both work transparently. Useful for staging forge inputs and retrieving forge outputs across machines. Forge outputs land at <root>\forge\<tool-name>\* and are also listed in the forge_call response as _outputs (each with an `uncPath` field for direct SMB access when uncShare is configured). TEMP / ROLLBACK AREA: <root>\temp\* is a scratch folder excluded from the VDB semantic index. Use it as a checkpoint area — before a risky edit, storage.copy the file to <root>\temp\<name>; to roll back, storage.copy it back over the live file. There is NO automatic versioning: the model owns its own snapshots via this folder. The VDB agent ignores the forge/, temp/, and _trash/ directories (config-level) and respects .nvdb_ignore files in any watched directory. TRASH: <root>\_trash\* holds soft-deleted items (layout _trash\<timestamp>\<original-path>). Prefer storage_delete with trash:true over permanent delete — it is reversible via storage_restore, and _trash stays out of the VDB index and storage_recent but remains fully listable/readable, so trashed content can be checked or recovered at any time. DISCOVERY: two complementary tools. (1) STRUCTURE — storage_list (compact by default: one line per entry, human sizes, summary header; detail:'full' for JSON with timestamps). Directories containing an Agents.md briefing are flagged (✓ in compact, hasAgents:true in full) — when you see the flag, READ that Agents.md FIRST: it holds directory-specific instructions for working inside that folder. Start shallow (recursive only when needed — compact render truncates at 2000 entries with a flag). (2) RECENT ACTIVITY — storage_recent answers 'what was recently worked on': the N most recently modified files under a path (default 20, newest first, with timestamps). It skips transient noise (nvdb/, forge/, temp/) by default. Use storage_recent to orient in a session ('what's live right now'), storage_list to map structure, storage_search (semantic) or storage_grep (regex) to find content.

tools.name: storage_stat
tools.description: Check if a path exists and what type it is (file or directory), without reading content. Returns exists, type, size, and modified time.

tools.name: storage_read
tools.description: Read a file from storage. Returns utf8 text by default; use encoding=base64 for binaries. RETURN SHAPE (utf8): the file content IS the response — verbatim plain text, complete, never truncated. A JSON object response is a POINTER, not content: inline:false means fetch the relative 'path' field (like /storage/somefile.md, no host — prepend your MCP server origin) over HTTP with your fetch tool; truncated:true means the file exceeds maxReadSize — page through it with offset+length windows. base64 results stay wrapped in a JSON envelope with size. To read only PART of a file, use EXACTLY ONE read-window (mutually exclusive): offset+length (byte window; offset REQUIRES length, never pass offset alone), head (first N lines), or tail (last N lines — strongly prefer for logs). Windowed utf8 results are also raw text. Spec-compliant alternative: storage files are also exposed as MCP resources via resources/read using storage://<relative-path>. Example: {"method":"storage_read","payload":{"path":"notes/idea.md"}}

offset.description: Byte offset for windowed read (REQUIRES length; mutually exclusive with head/tail)

length.description: Number of bytes to read from offset (only valid with offset)

head.description: Read first N lines (mutually exclusive with offset/length/tail)

tail.description: Read last N lines (mutually exclusive with offset/length/head)

tools.name: storage_write
tools.description: Write a file to storage. Creates parent directories automatically. Overwrites existing files. Content can be utf8 text or base64-encoded binary. Files above maxWriteSize are rejected. FULL-FILE REPLACEMENT only — content must be the ENTIRE file, not a section or fragment. For targeted edits use storage_replace (marker swap, server-side, no full content needed), for adding to the end use storage_append. The response is self-verifying: after writing, the server re-stats the file on disk and returns verified:true with size and mtime. If the post-write check fails, the call throws instead of returning ok — ok:true means the bytes are provably on disk. Example: {"method":"storage_write","payload":{"path":"notes/idea.md","content":"# My Idea\nHello world."}}.

content.description: File content (string for utf8, base64 string for binary)

tools.name: storage_list
tools.description: List a directory in storage (shallow by default — one level, cheap). COMPACT by default: one line per entry (d/f type, human-readable size, name; ✓ marks directories containing an Agents.md briefing — read that file first for directory-specific instructions before working inside it) plus a summary header — a fraction of the tokens of full JSON. detail:'full' returns the legacy JSON entries with timestamps. Use recursive=true only when you genuinely need all descendants as a flat list (can be huge; compact render is grouped by subdirectory, truncated with a flag at 2000 entries).

recursive.description: List all descendants as a flat list (default: false)

detail.description: compact (default): tree-style text, token-efficient; full: legacy JSON with modified timestamps

tools.name: storage_recent
tools.description: Answer 'what was recently worked on': the N most recently modified files under a path (default 20, newest first), rendered as compact text lines (timestamp, size, path). Skips transient noise directories (nvdb, forge, temp) by default — override with ignoreDirs:[]. Cheaper than recursive storage_list when you want current activity, not structure.

ignoreDirs.description: Directory names to skip anywhere in the tree (default: ['nvdb','forge','temp']); pass [] to include everything

tools.name: storage_move
tools.description: Move or rename a file or directory within storage. Refuses to overwrite an existing destination.

tools.name: storage_delete
tools.description: Delete a file or directory. DEFAULT IS PERMANENT. Prefer trash:true — SOFT DELETE: moves the item to _trash/<timestamp>/<original-path> (excluded from the VDB index and storage_recent; still listable/readable via normal storage tools) and returns a trashPath plus restorableVia pointer. Undo a trash with storage_restore; permanent delete of trashed items uses this tool without trash:true. Self-verifying: the response includes verified:true, confirming the path is gone from its original location.

path.description: Path to delete within storage root

recursive.description: Required to delete non-empty directories (default: false)

trash.description: Soft delete: move to _trash/<timestamp>/<original-path> instead of destroying. Reversible via storage_restore. (default: false)

tools.name: storage_restore
tools.description: Restore a trashed item to its original location. Accepts the trashPath returned by storage_delete trash:true (layout: _trash/<timestamp>/<original-path> — the segment after the timestamp IS the original path). If the original location is now occupied, restores under a .restored-<ts> suffix instead of overwriting. Inspect _trash contents first with storage_list {path:'_trash', recursive:true}.

path.description: Path inside _trash (from storage_delete trash response or _trash listing)

tools.name: storage_search
tools.description: Semantic search over files in storage using the vector database. Returns ranked matches with path, score, and optional content snippet. Filter by folder or file extension.

folder.description: Filter to a specific top-level folder in storage.

extension.description: Filter to files with this extension, e.g. '.md'.

top_k.description: Number of top matches to return.

include_content.description: Include the matched chunk text in results.

tools.name: storage_resources_list
tools.description: MCP Resources bridge: list all storage resources as MCP resource URIs. Returns paginated resources using the custom URI scheme storage://<relative-path>. Each resource has uri, name, mimeType, size, and annotations (directory: true for directories). Use the cursor field to page through large result sets. To read a resource, call storage_resources_read with its uri.

cursor.description: Pagination cursor from a previous response. Omit for the first page.

tools.name: storage_resources_read
tools.description: MCP Resources bridge: read the content of a storage resource by URI. Returns inline text for small files and a fetchable HTTP URL for files above the inline threshold (default 64 KB). For binary files, set encoding=base64. URI format: storage://<relative-path>. Find URIs with storage_resources_list or storage_resources_templates.

encoding.description: Content encoding (default: utf8 for text, base64 for binaries)

tools.name: storage_resources_templates
tools.description: MCP Resources bridge: list available resource URI templates. Currently exposes storage://{path} for arbitrary files under the storage root.

tools.name: storage_copy
tools.description: Copy a file or directory within storage, server-side. Content never enters your context — prefer this over read+write for duplicating or staging files. Refuses to overwrite unless overwrite:true. Self-verifying: the response includes verified:true, confirming the destination exists on disk (with size check for file copies).

overwrite.description: Allow overwriting an existing destination (default: false)

tools.name: storage_append
tools.description: Append content to a file (creates it if missing). O(1) — the existing file is NOT read into context. Use for logs, journals, growing notes. Self-verifying: the response re-stats the file on disk and includes verified:true with the new total size.

content.description: Content to append (utf8 text, or base64-encoded binary)

tools.name: storage_replace
tools.description: Replace text in a file server-side: finds a marker string and swaps it for the replacement, without the file content ever entering your context. The primary way to edit large files — no chunked reads, no read-modify-write round trip. Args: marker (alias: oldString), replacement (alias: newString), occurrence: 'first' (default), 'last', or 'all'. Throws with a DETAILED diagnostic if the marker is not found (file size, closest anchor position, line number, actual file snippet near the anchor) so you can repair the marker from the error alone — no blind retries. Pre-flight with storage_find if unsure whether the marker exists. Self-verifying: the response re-stats the file on disk and includes verified:true with the post-edit size — ok:true means the edit provably landed. Example: {"method":"storage_replace","payload":{"path":"a/b.md","marker":"old text","replacement":"new text"}}.

marker.description: Exact string to find (byte-exact, not a regex). Must uniquely identify the edit site unless occurrence is 'all'. Alias: oldString also accepted.

replacement.description: String to substitute in place of the marker. Alias: newString also accepted.

tools.name: storage_find
tools.description: Check whether an exact string exists in a file WITHOUT reading the file into your context and without changing anything. Returns { found, count, line, offset, snippet } — snippet shows the matching line so you can confirm it is the right occurrence. The pre-flight check for storage_replace: find first, replace only on found:true. For regex or multi-file search use storage_grep instead.

marker.description: Exact string to locate (byte-exact, not a regex). Aliases: oldString, pattern also accepted.

occurrence.description: Report position of first/last occurrence, or just the count for 'all' (default: first)

tools.name: storage_grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a regex, server-side. Returns only matching lines (path, line number, text, optional context lines) — file bodies never enter your context. The primary way to find text in storage. Skips binary and >50MB files. Set context:N for surrounding lines. path defaults to the storage root when omitted. Example: {"method":"storage_grep","payload":{"path":"docs/","pattern":"TODO|FIXME"}}.

path.description: File or directory path within storage root (default: storage root)

pattern.description: JavaScript regex pattern to match against each line

context.description: Number of surrounding lines to include before and after each match

tools.name: storage_batch
tools.description: Run multiple storage operations in ONE call. ops is an array of {op, ...args} where op is a storage op name (stat, read, write, list, move, remove, copy, append, readWindow, grep, hash, snapshotDir). Executes in order, returns per-op results. onError:'collect' (default) runs all; 'abort' stops at first failure. ⚡ BATCHING RULE: whenever your workflow touches MULTIPLE files (archive imports, multi-file updates, reorganizations), use ONE storage.batch or storage.import call — never one call per file. Each separate call costs a full round trip + model generation (~15s); a batch is milliseconds.

ops.description: Array of {op, ...args} objects. Each op is a storage operation name with its arguments as fields.

onError.description: collect (default): run all ops, return individual results; abort: stop at first error

tools.name: storage_import
tools.description: BULK WRITE — write MANY files in ONE call. files is an array of {path, content, encoding?}. PURPOSE-BUILT for archive workflows (e.g. writing an entire session's artifacts, a batch of notes, a set of generated files). Each file is written with the same atomic + self-verifying path as storage_write. Returns per-file verification, NOT content echo. ⚡ USE THIS when writing 2+ files — one import call replaces N storage_write calls and costs milliseconds instead of ~15s per file.

files.description: Array of {path, content, encoding?} objects. path is relative within storage root; content is the full file text (or base64 with encoding).

tools.name: storage_readMany
tools.description: BULK READ — read MANY files in ONE call. paths is an array of file paths. Returns per-file content (respects the same size threshold as storage_read — large files come back as a pointer). PURPOSE-BUILT for workflows that need several files at once (e.g. reading a plan + a scoreboard + a template). ⚡ USE THIS when reading 2+ files — one call replaces N storage_read calls.

paths.description: Array of relative paths within storage root
